parsed.summary: The passenger’s checked luggage was not delivered after a Tunisair flight from Paris to Tunis‑Carthage on 2026‑10‑17 and is now considered lost. Under Tunisair’s passenger protection rules and the Montreal Convention, the passenger must file a written claim within 21 days of the scheduled arrival, providing specific documents (PIR, baggage tag, boarding pass, ID, etc.) to avoid denial.

steps.action: Go to the Tunisair Lost & Found counter at Tunis‑Carthage Airport and request a Property Irregularity Report (PIR). Keep the original PIR and note the reference number.
Gather all required documents: original PIR, original baggage tag, boarding pass or ticket copy, a government‑issued ID, and a detailed description of the bag (color, brand, size, distinctive marks).

steps.when: Within 7 days of receiving the PIR (or no later than 21 days from the scheduled arrival)
steps.action: Draft a written claim addressed to Tunisair Customer Relations (see address in source [1]). Include the passenger’s contact details, flight information (flight number, date, Paris‑Tunis route), a summary of the loss, and attach all supporting documents collected.

steps.when: Within 10 days of drafting the claim
steps.action: Submit the claim via one of the following methods: • Online claim form on Tunisair’s website (https://www.tunisair.com/en/customer-care) • Certified postal mail to Tunisair Customer Relations Department, Charguia II, 2035 Tunis – Carthage, Tunisia. Retain proof of submission (email confirmation or postal receipt).
Monitor for a response from Tunisair. If no reply is received within 14 days, send a follow‑up email or letter referencing the original claim and requesting a status update.

steps.when: If the claim is denied or unsatisfactory
steps.action: Prepare to invoke the Montreal Convention (Art. 31 & Art. 17) by filing a complaint with the Tunisian Civil Aviation Authority or the relevant consumer protection body, attaching the same documentation and the Tunisair response.
